archetypes.name: temp-lifecycle
archetypes.rationale: The diff adds four new temp files in SKILL.md orchestration blocks (_argv_env, _argv_err_file, _init_stdout_file, _safe_init_env) each requiring cleanup on every exit path, plus trap-based cleanup in read-result-env.sh; leaked files containing sourced env vars are an operational risk the generic and edge-cases reviewers do not focus on.
archetypes.prompt_body: Trace every allocation of _argv_env, _argv_err_file, _init_stdout_file, and _safe_init_env in skills/design/SKILL.md Step 0-pre and Step 0b. For each temp file, enumerate every exit path (including early exits, set -e triggers, and sub-case branches) and verify the file is removed before the process exits. Then examine the trap/cleanup_tmp pattern in scripts/read-result-env.sh and the mktemp+mv pattern in skills/design/scripts/parse-design-argv.sh write_output_file() for races, partial-write exposure, and cleanup correctness when mv fails. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: combine-flow-logic
archetypes.rationale: The combine-issues SKILL.md adds a new four-state result from search-implementing-issue.sh (blocked/stale/ambiguous/none) and the helper uses gh issue list --limit 100 and jq contains() matching; subtle limit exhaustion, overly-broad substring matching, and fallback behavior on add-blocked-by.sh failure could silently misclassify items.
archetypes.prompt_body: In .claude/skills/combine-issues/scripts/search-implementing-issue.sh, check whether the --limit 100 cap causes STATUS=ambiguous when there are more than 100 open issues mentioning the path, and whether that is the correct behavior. Evaluate whether the jq contains($path) predicate could match unintended issue titles or bodies when SANITIZED_PATH is a short common substring. In the updated SKILL.md oos-2 step, verify that the fallback to STATUS=none when add-blocked-by.sh fails correctly keeps the item as actual (not blocked) and that this cannot cause the same item to appear in both blocked and active combination paths. Confirm the source-issue close guard in oos-5 correctly rejects closing when any items remain blocked, including the edge case where a source issue has all non-blocked items consumed but one blocked item. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: sourceable-env-protocol
archetypes.rationale: This diff introduces a new trust boundary where parse-design-argv.sh and read-result-env.sh write single-quote-encoded files that are then sourced by SKILL.md; variable name contract mismatches (lowercase vs uppercase bindings), encoding corner cases, and the PUBLIC_ARGV_WORDS stderr guard behavior after the redirection reordering deserve focused review.
archetypes.prompt_body: In skills/design/scripts/parse-design-argv.sh, verify that write_output_body correctly uses the lowercase script-local variable positional_kind when writing POSITIONAL_KIND= to the output file, and that SKILL.md sources POSITIONAL_KIND in uppercase as expected by the downstream case check. In SKILL.md Step 0-pre, the stderr guard checks _argv_err for the literal string PUBLIC_ARGV_WORDS; after the reordering (2>"$_argv_err_file" now precedes <PUBLIC_ARGV_WORDS>), determine whether a bash redirect-not-found error for the unexpanded placeholder would still contain the string PUBLIC_ARGV_WORDS and reach the guard. In scripts/read-result-env.sh, verify the ALLOW_KEYS heredoc mechanism inside is_allowed_key() produces the correct newline-separated list for multiple --allow invocations, and that the parse_env_file return-value convention (return 1 on malformed line) is correctly propagated through its caller. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
